verification.backend_test_root_cause: tests/test_endpoint_contracts.py's module fixture `client` did not isolate CACHE_DIR. For the unknown id 2099-nope-fire-000000, catalog.resolve_listed checks the live list and then one WFIGS `IrwinID LIKE '{000000%'` lookup, both through fire3d.http's disk cache in data/cache. Suppose the live list is fresh there (CAL FIRE 10 min TTL, refreshed by any running dev server) and the cached WFIGS answer is older than its 24 h TTL (it was written Oct 23 02:36). Then the lookup reaches conftest's blocked transport, resolve_listed records a failed lookup and raises ListsUnavailable, and the API answers 503. Reproduced: 503 right after this step's API fetched the live list. With the fix (empty temp CACHE_DIR + catalog.clear_cache() before and after) the file passes in that same state (17 passed), and so does the full suite (1009 passed). Note: with an empty cache the 404 comes from conftest's refusal raising RuntimeError (not an httpx error), which app._catalog_summary treats as 'not listed'; a real outage (HttpError) still answers 503 by design (CONTRACT 14.2).

user_summary:
Brief 4 is finished and checked. Here is what changed, in plain words.

What changed in each view
- Public, all fires: the map opens clean. You see a search bar in the middle, a round 'find me' button beside it, small map buttons on the right and one disclaimer line at the bottom. Each fire is an orange outlined circle; crowded areas show one bigger circle that says how many fires it holds ('28 FIRES'); the biggest fires have their names on short lines. 'Show details' (bottom right) brings back the full list of fires, the official fire-weather notices and the legend.
- Public, one fire: click any fire and you get a simple fire page. A big glowing circle shows the fire's name and what the agency says about it (for example ACTIVE or DECLARED OUT). Beside it are the official facts (acres burned, percent contained, start date, fire-weather warnings, evacuation zones, last official update), each with its source and time. The map shows only the newest official fire outline. There is no prediction here on purpose; 'MORE IN COMMAND' takes you to it.
- Command: everything it had before, laid out like the design. Your selected point and what is known there is on the left, 'Official now' on the right (click a line to read the full official wording), and a thin timeline along the bottom.
- Forensic (3D): the same 3D scene and tools, in the new grey and orange colours, with the view switch in the top bar.
- In Public and Command the edges of the map darken in a circle as you zoom in, like the edge of a globe, so the middle stays bright.
- Every view still says 'Research prototype — not for operational use' and 'Not an all-clear. Follow local officials.'

How to turn (rotate) the map, in all three views
- Press E to turn right 15 degrees, Q to turn left, N to point north up again.
- Or click the two curved-arrow buttons next to the compass.
- Or drag the compass needle around in a circle; a single click on it points north up.
- Or hold Ctrl and drag the map (or drag with the right mouse button).
- The direction you chose stays when you switch between 2D and 3D, or between Command and Forensic.

What to try on your Mac
- In Safari, put two fingers on the trackpad and twist: the map should turn. Chrome on a Mac has no trackpad twist, so use Q / E, the buttons or the compass there. This is the one thing we could not test in the cloud.
- Open a fire in Public, then press 'MORE IN COMMAND' and back, and click 'Share your location' to see how far you are (your location stays in your browser).
- Turn on 'Reduce motion' in macOS settings (Accessibility > Display): the glowing circle and every other animation should stand still.

What is left for later
- Search suggestions as you type (towns, ZIP codes, fire names), searching for a fire inside Forensic, the globe intro page, and a second experimental prediction model (Wildfire-FM).
- Small things: on phones some Forensic buttons are smaller than ideal, and Command's map buttons take two rows; the details are in this report's known issues.
